title: TukaBench: A Culturally Grounded Jailbreak Benchmark for African Languages

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM safety behaviors (Attack Success Rate, Refusal Rate, and Deflection Rate) when processing harmful and benign jailbreak prompts in English versus seven low-resource African languages (Amharic, Hausa, Igbo, Chichewa, Swahili, Yoruba, and isiXhosa).

Evaluating differences in jailbreak susceptibility by comparing model responses to directly translated Western-centric prompts against culturally adapted prompts that incorporate African named entities, local governance structures, and regional harms.

Measuring discrepancies in prompt comprehension and deflection rates between Latin-script African languages and Amharic, which utilizes the non-Latin Ge'ez script, to identify tokenization-related performance disparities.
